title: Password Wizard: 4D v11 SQL Component for the Creation and Management of Passwords
author: Charles “Charlie” Vass, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note explains password entropy theory and provides a self-contained 4D component for generating, rating, and encrypting passwords for storage as BLOBs in a 4D data file. The underlying cryptographic and entropy concepts are timeless and the classic-language component would still technically function, but modern secure-password practice has moved toward standardized, vetted algorithms (bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2, or platform-provided credential/keychain APIs) rather than a bespoke home-grown key-pair/BLOB scheme, and 4D now offers built-in encryption commands unavailable in 2010. Developers building new authentication today should prefer current cryptographic libraries and 4D's built-in security features over this legacy component.
related_updates: Modern 4D applications typically use vetted hashing algorithms (bcrypt/Argon2) and 4D's newer built-in encryption/hash commands rather than this custom component
4D's built-in CryptoKey/Verify password and related security commands introduced in later versions supersede bespoke password-strength tooling
